title.en: AN ACT DEFINING HIGHWAY ROBBERY OR BRIGANDAGE, AND PROVIDING FOR THE PUNISHMENT THEREFOR.
title.orig: AN ACT DEFINING HIGHWAY ROBBERY OR BRIGANDAGE, AND PROVIDING FOR THE PUNISHMENT THEREFOR.

source.name: The LawPhil Project — Arellano Law Foundation

completenessNote: 全文，共 6 条；逐字取自 LawPhil PDF 文本化成果（第三方 OCR，非机翻），原始文件 ACT_00518_1902_html.txt

text.en:
Whenever three or more persons, conspiring together, shall form a hand of robbers for the purpose
of stealing carabao or other personal property, by means of force and violence, and shall go out upon the
highway or roam over the country, armed with deadly weapons for this purpose, they shall be deemed
highway robbers or brigands, and every person engaged in the original formation of the band, or joining it
thereafter, shall, upon conviction thereof, be punished by death or imprisonment for not less than twenty
years, in the discretion of the court.

To prove the crime described in the previous section, it shall not be necessary to adduce evidence
that any member of the hand has in fact committed robbery or theft, but it shall be sufficient to justify
conviction thereunder if, from the circumstances, it can be inferred beyond reasonable doubt that the accused
was a member of such an armed band as that described in said section.

Persons guilty of the crime defined in section one may be punished therefor in the Court of First
Instance in any province; in which they may be taken or from which they may have fled.

Every person knowingly aiding or abetting such a band of brigands as that described in section
one by giving them information of the movement of the police or constabulary, or by securing stolen
property from them, or by procuring supplies of food, clothing, arms, or ammunition and furnishing the same
to thorn shall upon conviction, be punished by imprisonment for not loss than ten years and not more than
twenty years.

The public good requiring bill, the passage, of the same is hereby section two of "An Act
prescribing the order of procedure by the Commission in the enactment of law," passed September twenty-
sixth, nineteen hundred.

This Act shall take effect on its passage.
Enacted, November 12, 1902.
